note: A blank field means nobody has verified it yet. It does not mean no. This matters most for hazards and dams.
sources: Lower Haw River State Natural Area

spots.name: Bass Lake Park
spots.managing_agency: Town of Holly Springs Parks and Recreation
spots.notes_public: A small 50 acre lake with a two mile loop trail around it. Rentals do not include boards, so bring your own.
spots.rentals: Canoes and rowboats, plus a Gheenoe with a trolling motor. Hirers must be 16 or over. Seven days a week from Memorial Day to Labor Day. No paddleboards listed.

spots.name: Blythe Landing Park
spots.fee_permit: Launch fee applies. Season passes available.
spots.notes_public: A busy trailer ramp with 218 trailer spaces, so expect motorboats. The nonprofit sailing centre on site is the interesting part for paddlers, offering the cheapest membership route onto this lake.
spots.private_launch: Yes for private boats. Only county-approved hire companies may launch commercially.
spots.rentals: Lake Norman Community Sailing, a nonprofit sailing centre, runs from here and its family membership covers kayaking and paddleboarding as well as sailing.

spots.name: Bynum Dam Access, US 15-501
spots.fee_permit: None
spots.park_name: Lower Haw River State Natural Area
spots.hazards: Bynum Dam. Put in above the dam only. Never approach a dam face from upstream.
spots.low_head_dam: Yes, Bynum Dam sits immediately downstream of this put-in
spots.flow_high_cfs: 5.7 ft on the Bynum gauge, open-boat limit set by Haw River Assembly
spots.notes_public: Flat for about a mile upstream of the dam, which makes this the gentlest water on the Lower Haw. Stay above the dam.

spots.name: Bynum Mill Access
spots.fee_permit: None
spots.park_name: Lower Haw River State Natural Area
spots.hazards: Downstream of Bynum Dam. Intermediate to advanced water.
spots.flow_high_cfs: 5.7 ft on the Bynum gauge, open-boat limit set by Haw River Assembly
spots.notes_public: 160 Bynum Church Road. This is the only developed, official paddle launch State Parks maintains in the whole state natural area. Everything else here is undeveloped.

spots.name: Copperhead Island
spots.fee_permit: Launch fee applies
spots.notes_public: A 14 acre island park across the water from McDowell Nature Preserve. Quiet in the morning, busier once the trailers arrive. Six tent sites make it one of very few paddle-and-camp options this close to Charlotte.
spots.private_launch: Yes

spots.name: Eno River Access at Red Mill Road
spots.notes_public: Off Red Mill Road near Teknika Parkway in eastern Durham County. Deep flatwater, described as the most accessible launch on the Eno. Two miles upstream to the Little River confluence, two miles down to Falls Lake.

spots.name: Eno River SP, Cole Mill Access
spots.fee_permit: None for day use
spots.hazards: Rapids appear above roughly 2.25 ft on the Eno gauges.
spots.flow_low_cfs: Below 3 ft on the Eno gauges runs shallow
spots.flow_high_cfs: Above 5 ft is beyond most paddlers' ability to self rescue
spots.notes_public: Six miles of trail and a Cole Mill Road gauge nearby, so you can check the level for this exact stretch before driving out.

spots.name: Eno River SP, Fews Ford Access
spots.fee_permit: None for day use
spots.hazards: Rapids appear above roughly 2.25 ft on the Eno gauges. Swift and often shallow.
spots.flow_low_cfs: Below 3 ft on the Eno gauges runs shallow, harder in a canoe than a kayak
spots.flow_high_cfs: Above 5 ft the river leaves its banks and moves beyond most paddlers' ability to self rescue
spots.notes_public: Visitor centre access with the largest trail network in the park. The park itself describes the Eno as swift but often shallow, which makes paddling here level-dependent rather than reliable.

spots.name: Falls Lake SRA, Beaverdam Access
spots.notes_public: The park lists Beaverdam as non-gas boating, which is why it stays calm on a summer weekend. Accessible fishing and swim beach.
spots.private_launch: Yes, at public ramps and designated launch sites only

spots.name: Hanging Rock SP, Dan River Access
spots.notes_public: Dedicated paddling access on the Dan, linked to the main park area by the Indian Creek Trail.

spots.name: Jordan Lake SRA, Crosswinds Campground
spots.fee_permit: Per vehicle on weekends and holidays in April, May and September, and daily from Memorial Day to Labor Day
spots.dogs_allowed: Yes, leashed to 6 ft. Not allowed on swim beaches or inside buildings.
spots.notes_public: Boat ramp and swim beach are for campers only. A privately owned marina sits nearby.
spots.private_launch: Yes, at public ramps and designated launch sites only
spots.rentals: Privately owned marina nearby hires fishing boats, kayaks and paddleboards

spots.name: Jordan Lake SRA, Ebenezer Church Access
spots.fee_permit: Per vehicle on weekends and holidays in April, May and September, and daily from Memorial Day to Labor Day
spots.dogs_allowed: Yes, leashed to 6 ft. Not allowed on swim beaches or inside buildings.
spots.notes_public: Named by the park as the best access for windsurfing, which tells you it catches wind. Accessible swim beach and picnic shelters on site.
spots.private_launch: Yes, at public ramps and designated launch sites only

spots.name: Jordan Lake SRA, New Hope Overlook Access
spots.fee_permit: Per vehicle on weekends and holidays in April, May and September, and daily from Memorial Day to Labor Day
spots.dogs_allowed: Yes, leashed to 6 ft. Not allowed on swim beaches or inside buildings.
spots.notes_public: Day-use ramps plus short hike-in backpack camping. The quietest corner of the lake.
spots.private_launch: Yes, at public ramps and designated launch sites only

spots.name: Jordan Lake SRA, Parkers Creek Access
spots.fee_permit: Per vehicle on weekends and holidays in April, May and September, and daily from Memorial Day to Labor Day
spots.dogs_allowed: Yes, leashed to 6 ft. Not allowed on swim beaches or inside buildings.
spots.notes_public: Tent, trailer and RV sites with some hookups, plus walk-up only loops and group camping. Swim beach and picnic shelters.
spots.private_launch: Yes, at public ramps and designated launch sites only

spots.name: Jordan Lake SRA, Poplar Point Campground
spots.fee_permit: Per vehicle on weekends and holidays in April, May and September, and daily from Memorial Day to Labor Day
spots.dogs_allowed: Yes, leashed to 6 ft. Not allowed on swim beaches or inside buildings.
spots.notes_public: Campers-only boat ramp and docks. Walk-up loops mean you can sometimes get a site without booking.
spots.private_launch: Yes, at public ramps and designated launch sites only

spots.name: Jordan Lake SRA, Seaforth Access
spots.fee_permit: Per vehicle on weekends and holidays in April, May and September, and daily from Memorial Day to Labor Day
spots.dogs_allowed: Yes, leashed to 6 ft. Not allowed on swim beaches or inside buildings.
spots.notes_public: Wide open view of the lake, which is scenic and also means very little shelter from wind.
spots.private_launch: Yes, at public ramps and designated launch sites only

spots.name: Jordan Lake SRA, Vista Point Access
spots.fee_permit: Per vehicle on weekends and holidays in April, May and September, and daily from Memorial Day to Labor Day
spots.dogs_allowed: Yes, leashed to 6 ft. Not allowed on swim beaches or inside buildings.
spots.notes_public: Group camping only, both RV and tent. Sailboat launch and swim beach.
spots.private_launch: Yes, at public ramps and designated launch sites only

spots.name: Jordan Lake SRA, White Oak Recreation Area
spots.fee_permit: Per vehicle on weekends and holidays in April, May and September, and daily from Memorial Day to Labor Day
spots.hours: 9am to 5pm weekdays. Closed Saturday and Sunday.
spots.dogs_allowed: Yes, leashed to 6 ft. Not allowed on swim beaches or inside buildings.
spots.notes_public: Open for day use in peak season only when the rental facility is not booked, so call ahead before driving out.
spots.private_launch: Yes, at public ramps and designated launch sites only

spots.name: Kerr Lake SRA, Bullocksville Access
spots.notes_public: Accessible fishing pier, concession stand and a short hiking loop. No boat ramp listed by the park.
spots.private_launch: Yes, at public ramps and designated launch sites only

spots.name: Kerr Lake SRA, County Line Access
spots.parking_spaces: Two ramps with parking described as somewhat tight
spots.notes_public: Open sailing water with camping and group sites.
spots.private_launch: Yes, at public ramps and designated launch sites only

spots.name: Kerr Lake SRA, Henderson Point Access
spots.notes_public: Accessible fishing pier and a swim area. Good sailing water, which means it is open and can get choppy.
spots.private_launch: Yes, at public ramps and designated launch sites only

spots.name: Kerr Lake SRA, Hibernia Access
spots.notes_public: Longest trail in the park runs from here, along with a swim area and group camping.
spots.private_launch: Yes, at public ramps and designated launch sites only

spots.name: Kerr Lake SRA, J.C. Cooper Campground
spots.notes_public: Ramp and dock are campers only. Sits within the Satterwhite Point access.
spots.private_launch: Yes, at public ramps and designated launch sites only

spots.name: Kerr Lake SRA, Kimball Point Access
spots.notes_public: Swim beach and camping. Named by the park as good sailing water, so read the wind before you go.
spots.private_launch: Yes, at public ramps and designated launch sites only

spots.name: Kerr Lake SRA, Nutbush Bridge Access
spots.notes_public: Two ramps, one sized for fishing tournaments. Expect heavy trailer traffic on tournament weekends.
spots.private_launch: Yes, at public ramps and designated launch sites only

spots.name: Kerr Lake SRA, Satterwhite Point Access
spots.notes_public: Visitor centre, the park's only designated swim beach, and a privately owned marina. The busiest access on the lake.
spots.swim_area_here: Yes, the only designated swim beach in the park
spots.private_launch: Yes, at public ramps and designated launch sites only

spots.name: Lake Benson Boat House
spots.managing_agency: Town of Garner Parks and Recreation
spots.dogs_allowed: No, pets are not permitted on boathouse craft
spots.notes_public: Worth reading twice before you drive out. You cannot put your own boat on this lake at all, only boathouse craft, and the boathouse opens weekends only. A shallow, quiet lake if you are happy in a hired kayak.
spots.private_launch: No. Boathouse craft only.
spots.rentals: Jon boats, kayaks and canoes from the boathouse. Trolling motor available.

spots.name: Lake Crabtree County Park
spots.managing_agency: Wake County Parks, Recreation and Open Space
spots.notes_public: Free boat hire, which is rare, and that includes paddleboards. Demand is heavy at weekends and in good weather, so paddlers advise arriving about half an hour before opening.
spots.private_launch: Yes, year-round launch area
spots.rentals: Canoes, kayaks, rowboats, pedal boats and paddleboards, free of charge with valid ID

spots.name: Lake Johnson Park
spots.managing_agency: City of Raleigh Parks and Recreation
spots.walk_to_water: Paddlers report hauling boats from the far end of the car park when the near lot fills.
spots.parking_spaces: Two car parks, both of which fill early at weekends
spots.notes_public: A 150 acre lake close to NC State, calm and well liked by beginners. Parking is the real constraint. Arrive early at a weekend or you will be carrying your board a long way.
spots.private_launch: Yes
spots.rentals: Kayaks and paddleboards from WakeRack lockers by the Waterfront Center. Pedal boats, canoes and fishing boats through the park.

spots.name: Lake Michie Park and Marina
spots.hours: 6:30am to 6pm Friday through Monday. Closed Tuesday, Wednesday and Thursday.
spots.notes_public: One of the very few launches in the region with an ADA accessible boat house, dock and canoe/kayak launch. Non-motorized only, covering canoes, kayaks, paddleboards and sailboats, so it stays quiet.

spots.name: Lake Norman State Park
spots.notes_public: Largest manmade lake in the state with 520 miles of shoreline. Boat rentals, swim beach and cabins. Check the DEQ algal bloom dashboard here in summer.
spots.private_launch: Yes, at public ramps and designated launch sites only

spots.name: Lake Norman YMCA Lake Access
spots.hours: Lake access is seasonal and limited, historically summer Saturdays only. Ring before going.
spots.notes_public: A supervised cove with lifeguards on the water and life jackets required, which makes it one of the gentlest introductions to a board anywhere on Lake Norman. Equipment is free but you need a Y membership, and lake access hours are far shorter than the building's.
spots.private_launch: Members only. Nationwide YMCA memberships are accepted.
spots.rentals: Canoes, kayaks and paddleboards provided free to members, plus inflatables in the cove

spots.name: Lake Wheeler Park
spots.managing_agency: City of Raleigh Parks and Recreation
spots.launch_type: Ramp for trailered and hand-carried boats
spots.fee_permit: Daily or annual launch pass required, about $6 a day for non-residents
spots.hours: 6am to 8pm. Boats must be off the water 30 minutes before sunset or closing, whichever is first.
spots.motorized_allowed: Yes, no jet skis. 40 mph limit, and skiing and tubing are permitted.
spots.notes_public: A 650 acre water supply lake, and the clearest example of flat water that is not swimmable. Swimming and wading are both banned, and motorboats can run at 40 mph with skiers behind them. Fine for a confident paddler, a poor choice for a first time on a board.
spots.swimming_allowed: No. Swimming and wading are both prohibited.
spots.private_launch: Yes, with a launch pass
spots.rentals: Kayaks and paddleboards from WakeRack self-service lockers near the Waterfront Center, booked online

spots.name: Latta Nature Preserve
spots.notes_public: Mountain Island Lake is smaller and far less trafficked than Lake Norman, with much less motor traffic. Forested and undeveloped, and a good choice when the big lake is churned up.
spots.private_launch: Yes
spots.rentals: Mountain Island Lake Paddle Company will deliver boards and kayaks to the launches

spots.name: Little River Fishing Facility
spots.hours: 6:30am to 6pm Monday, Friday, Saturday and Sunday. Closed Tuesday, Wednesday and Thursday.
spots.notes_public: Rental only, like Lake Benson. You cannot launch your own boat here, and it is shut three days a week. Restrooms on site, no bait sold.
spots.private_launch: No. Hired craft only, and private trolling motors are not permitted.
spots.rentals: Kayaks, canoes and jon boats with trolling motors. Bring your own battery.

spots.name: Mayo River SP, Anglin Mill Access
spots.notes_public: Mayo Beach and the Boiling Hole are here. No restrooms, so plan around that.

spots.name: Mayo River SP, Mayodan Access
spots.notes_public: Put in on the Mayo and paddle down into the Dan.

spots.name: McDowell Nature Preserve
spots.fee_permit: Free entry
spots.camping_type: Drive-in, small RV area with electric and water
spots.notes_public: One of the few Mecklenburg sites that explicitly welcomes your own board, launching from the landing by the waterfront deck. Nature centre, forested trails and quiet lake views.
spots.private_launch: Yes, bring your own canoe, kayak or paddleboard
spots.rentals: None for hire, but guided programmes provide boats

spots.name: Medoc Mountain State Park
spots.notes_public: The park calls this one of the cleanest streams in the region. Quiet paddling with almost no boat traffic.
spots.private_launch: Yes, at public ramps and designated launch sites only

spots.name: Morrow Mountain State Park
spots.notes_public: Sits where Lake Tillery meets the Yadkin, under the Uwharrie peaks. Boat rentals on site and bald eagles overhead.
spots.private_launch: Yes, at public ramps and designated launch sites only

spots.name: Mt Holly Boat Landing
spots.managing_agency: Privately owned, Aquatic Adventures operates from here
spots.fee_permit: About $2 per person to launch a boat, canoe or kayak
spots.hazards: Sits just below the Mountain Island Lake dam. Flow changes when the dam releases.
spots.notes_public: Private land, and worth every bit of the two dollars. Just south of the Mountain Island dam on a wide, quiet stretch. The run downstream is about 2.75 miles through tree-lined water with almost no development or boat traffic. Rocks show through when the current is up.
spots.private_launch: Yes, for a small per person fee
spots.rentals: Kayaks and paddleboards on site. Aquatic Adventures runs guided trips and full moon paddles from here.

spots.name: Old Bynum Bridge Access
spots.fee_permit: None
spots.park_name: Lower Haw River State Natural Area
spots.hazards: Downstream of Bynum Dam. Intermediate to advanced water.
spots.flow_high_cfs: 5.7 ft on the Bynum gauge, open-boat limit set by Haw River Assembly
spots.notes_public: Parking on the east side of Bynum Road. Downstream from here to US 64 is rated by the state natural area for intermediate to advanced paddlers only.

spots.name: Pilot Mountain SP, Ivy Bluff Access
spots.walk_to_water: Roughly half a mile of trail from the car park down to the river. Smooth surface and a gradual slope, but it is a long way to carry a hard board.
spots.notes_public: Parking for paddle-in campers, with steep riverside slopes on the hiking approach.

spots.name: Pilot Mountain SP, Shoals Fishing Area
spots.notes_public: Paddling launch for the Yadkin, doubling as a fishing access.

spots.name: Ramsey Creek Park
spots.fee_permit: Launch fee applies
spots.ada_launch: No, but there is an ADA compliant fishing pier
spots.dogs_allowed: Yes, there is a dog park at the entrance
spots.notes_public: A seasonal lifeguarded beach, four ramps and a dog park. The shoreline is rocky, so water shoes help. Check beach dates before relying on it.
spots.private_launch: Yes

spots.name: Raven Rock State Park
spots.notes_public: The park explicitly names rapids on the Cape Fear here, plus the remains of the Northington Lock and Dam. Scout before you run it and check the class rating against current flow.
spots.private_launch: Yes, at public ramps and designated launch sites only

spots.name: Robeson Creek Boat Ramp
spots.fee_permit: None
spots.flow_high_cfs: 5.7 ft on the Bynum gauge, open-boat limit set by Haw River Assembly
spots.notes_public: A full trailer ramp run by the Wildlife Resources Commission, so expect motorboats. Paddle about a mile down Robeson Creek to reach the Haw.

spots.name: Robeson Creek Canoe Access
spots.fee_permit: None
spots.park_name: Lower Haw River State Natural Area
spots.flow_high_cfs: 5.7 ft on the Bynum gauge, open-boat limit set by Haw River Assembly
spots.notes_public: Despite the name this launch is on the Haw, not on Robeson Creek. Flat for a short way upstream and flat for a long way downstream all the way to Jordan Lake, which makes it the best board-friendly put-in on the Lower Haw.

spots.name: South Bynum River Access
spots.walk_to_water: Long. Recommended approach is to park on the east side of the historic Bynum Bridge and walk across the bridge.
spots.fee_permit: None
spots.park_name: Lower Haw River State Natural Area
spots.hazards: Downstream of Bynum Dam. Intermediate to advanced water.
spots.flow_high_cfs: 5.7 ft on the Bynum gauge, open-boat limit set by Haw River Assembly
spots.notes_public: Formerly Bynum Beach Canoe Access. Parking is extremely limited and roadside parking on Bynum Beach Road is expressly prohibited, so plan on the bridge walk with your board.

spots.name: Tailrace Marina
spots.notes_public: Near the mouth of Dutchman's Creek where it meets Lake Wylie. Online booking and waivers mean you can be on the water quickly. A long-standing Catawba Riverkeeper Riversweep site.
spots.rentals: Kayaks, paddleboards, canoes and pontoons. An annual kayak membership covers a guest.

spots.name: U.S. National Whitewater Center
spots.fee_permit: Around $39 for a day of flatwater kayaking and paddleboarding, plus about $13 to park
spots.notes_public: The flatwater paddling here is on the Catawba and Long Creek and is separate from the artificial whitewater channel. Everything is an added fee, so read the pricing before you go.
spots.private_launch: Unknown, the site is built around its own hire fleet
spots.rentals: Flatwater kayaks and paddleboards included in the activity pass. Life jacket provided.

spots.name: US 64 Haw River Canoe Access
spots.parking_spaces: Large gravel lot at 348 River Access Road, plus a very small gravel lot on the south east side and roadside parking on the north west service road
spots.fee_permit: None
spots.park_name: Lower Haw River State Natural Area
spots.hazards: The state natural area rates the run downstream of here for experts only.
spots.flow_high_cfs: 5.7 ft on the Bynum gauge, open-boat limit set by Haw River Assembly
spots.notes_public: Experts only heading downstream toward Robeson Creek. The classic Lower Haw whitewater run starts here and it is not a beginner stretch.

spots.name: West Point on the Eno
spots.hazards: Mill dam at the historic mill. Put in above the dam.
spots.low_head_dam: Yes, the mill dam. Launch above it.
spots.notes_public: Enter above the dam behind the mill and paddle roughly three quarters of a mile up to Sennet Hole. The dam holds deep water year round, so this is one of the few Eno spots that does not depend on rain.

spots.name: William B. Umstead SP, Crabtree Creek Access
spots.notes_public: Big Lake and Sycamore Lake, with boat rentals on site. Nine miles from downtown Raleigh and it feels much further.
spots.private_launch: Yes, at public ramps and designated launch sites only

spots.name: William B. Umstead SP, Reedy Creek Access
spots.notes_public: Small lake with a millstone marker from an old grist mill. Group campsites and a stone-deck picnic shelter.
spots.private_launch: Yes, at public ramps and designated launch sites only
